expected_differences: Demo Coffee Co. in Raleigh replaces the Lab’s fictional Loopday Coffee identity and Austin context; the account email and business details reflect production records.
The identity switcher shows the actual personal account and three businesses, using supplied business imagery or initial fallbacks rather than invented portraits.
Connected integrations, the approved brand kit, active subscription, notification preference and “Only you” team summary replace discovery fixtures with relevant current conditions.
Plan and billing explicitly describes the subscription and keeps campaign credit separate. Discovery asking prices and creator payouts do not belong in this Settings summary.
Contact support is correctly absent because no support mailbox is configured.
keep: The mineral canvas, flat utility rows and restrained dividers; graphite remains concentrated in the navigation rail rather than becoming decorative Settings panels.
The shared 200px rail, 32px main-content gutter, restrained TapMart mark and clearly selected Business navigation item.
The strong Settings heading, readable operational labels and supporting metadata hierarchy.
The account/business grouping alongside a separate identity-switching and session-management column.
Literal Connected, Approved, Active and Current labels, with ink secondary actions and a clearly distinguished Log out action.
The absence of a decorative source-to-commitment offset: these management rows contain no source object requiring that joint.
review.readiness_note: Sign off for visual release at desktop 1440. The supplied Lab image is Business Home, not a Settings fixture, so this is a system-transfer assessment. The capture preserves the visible management destinations and identity/session controls; navigation, switching and backend mutations still require functional testing.
review.why: The production screen carries the Lab’s warm neutral field, graphite rail, typography hierarchy and flat construction into an appropriately quieter utility layout. The main list begins at x232, preserving the desktop gutter; its roughly 64px rows provide comfortable separation without card-grid styling. Current conditions sit beneath row titles or align at the trailing edge, keeping destinations easy to scan. Business remains selected in the rail, while the back link retains management context. Account, Notifications, Security, Business details, Connections, Google Business, Brand kit, Plan and billing, Team and Public page remain exposed. The side column preserves identity switching, Add a business and device-scoped logout explanation. Small identity images and initials are sufficient here; there is no missing hero or media assembly. No material visual drift or capture-visible functional regression is evident.
review.verdict: Frame Shift has been faithfully transferred to desktop Settings, with clear production states and no visible loss of management functionality.
